claims.excerpt: Selective Availability: Two Separate GPS Changes
claims.claim: The piece presents two distinct GPS changes involving Selective Availability: stopping its use and omitting it from a future generation.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: In May 2000 the US government stopped using it at President Bill Clinton’s direction to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. In September 2007 the government announced it would procure the future GPS III generation without the feature.
claims.narrative: The story distinguishes two changes to Selective Availability, the feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security.
claims.explanation: The title’s distinction matches the separate 2000 operational change and 2007 procurement announcement in the source.
claims.materiality: Frames the central distinction of the piece.
